pages.text:
LEARNING OBJECTIVES

Understand key elements of a persuasive demand packet

Align medical summaries and damages with case theory

Anticipate and address common defense arguments

pages.title: What is a DEMAND PACKET?
pages.text:
What is a DEMAND PACKET?

A DEMAND PACKET is a written document that explains why someone is responsible for an incident and details the damages suffered. It organizes all facts, evidence, and legal points to support the claim and aim for a settlement before trial.

pages.title: Key Elements
pages.text:
Key Elements:

1. Demand Letter
2. Case Summary
3. Legal Basis
4. Evidence of Liability
5. Medical Records and Summaries
6. Bills and Financial Documentation
7. Damages Statement
8. Exhibits / Supporting Documents

Before we can send a DEMAND LETTER, you must have a complete understanding of the client’s accident, injuries, damages, and value.

pages.title: Evidence Checklists
pages.text:
Evidence Checklists:

1. Police Report
2. Vehicle Estimate
Only include if the value is more than $1,000
3. PIP Log
Should not be more than 60 days old
4. EMS Report and Bill
5. Emergency Room Report
6. Chiropractic Report
7. Physical Therapy Report
8. Orthopedic Report
9. Pain Management Report
10. Imaging
11. Surgery
12. Emergency Medical Condition
13. Any prior Medical Records

Make sure to use the correct naming convention to reflect the chronology.

pages.title: Demand Response
pages.text:
Demand
Response

is the opposing party’s formal reply to your demand packet. Understanding it is key to evaluating settlement posture, spotting weaknesses, and deciding next steps. Below is a complete, practical guide from receipt to strategy.

What a Demand Response Is (and Isn’t)

What it is
The recipient’s written position on liability, damages, and settlement value.
A negotiation document that frames their defenses and willingness to resolve.
What it isn’t
Not an admission of liability.
Not binding unless a settlement is agreed to in writing.

pages.title: Forms of a Demand Response
pages.text:
Full Acceptance

Agrees to your demand amount.
Rare; usually followed by release paperwork.

Forms of a Demand Response

Counteroffer

Most common.
Accepts some liability/damages but disputes value.

Partial Denial

Accepts liability but disputes damages (or vice versa).

Complete Denial

Denies liability and/or causation entirely.

pages.title: Common Arguments You’ll See
pages.text:
Liability Defenses

Common Arguments You’ll See

Comparative or contributory negligence
Lack of evidence / conflicting accounts
No duty or no breach

Causation Defenses

Pre-existing conditions
Gap in treatment
Delayed onset of symptoms
Unrelated or degenerative findings

Damages Disputes

Excessive or unnecessary treatment
Inflated medical bills
Low-impact / “minor damage” argument
Disputing permanency or future care
Lost wages not substantiated

pages.title: How to Review a Demand Response
pages.text:
How to Review a Demand Response

Calendar Deadlines

Note any response deadlines or expiration of offers.

Break Down Their Position

What do they accept?
What do they dispute?
What evidence do they rely on?

Compare Against Your Demand

Identify gaps between their valuation and yours.
Note any issues you didn’t fully address
in your packet.

Spot Leverage Points

Weak defenses
Admissions

pages.title: Evaluating a Counteroffer
pages.text:
Evaluating a Counteroffer

CONSIDER:

Strength of liability
Quality and consistency of medical treatment
Jurisdictional tendencies
Policy limits
Client’s goals and risk tolerance
Litigation costs vs. settlement delta

pages.title: Drafting Demand Response Reply
pages.text:
Drafting Demand Response Reply

When replying:

Stay professional and factual
Directly address each disputed issue
Attach only relevant supplemental exhibits
Re-anchor value with facts, not emotion
Clearly state your new demand or position
Set a reasonable deadline

pages.title: Red Flags to Watch For
pages.text:
Red to Watch For

Boilerplate denial with no case-specific analysis
Ignoring key evidence you provided
Repeated requests for already-sent documents
Offers far below documented specials without explanation

pages.title: How Demand Responses Affect Litigation
pages.text:
How Demand Responses Affect Litigation

Can be used to show reasonableness of settlement efforts

May support or undermine bad faith arguments (jurisdiction-dependent)

Helps shape pleadings, discovery, and expert strategy
